content.title: About
content.content: Tea with ginger is an aromatic beverage made from black (or green) tea leaves flavored with dried ginger. It combines the brisk taste of tea with the spicy warmth of ginger, making it popular both hot and cold.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ginger has been used in traditional Chinese and Indian medicine for over 5,000 years.
Tea and ginger pair is common in Asian cultures, where ginger tea is considered a warming drink.
Ginger tea is often served with honey or lemon to enhance flavor and benefits.
Dried ginger retains most of its active compounds, including gingerol.
In some countries ginger tea is sold in ready‑to‑use tea bags, while in others it is offered as loose leaf.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Ginger has anti‑inflammatory and antioxidant properties that may help strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Improved digestion
items.content: Ginger stimulates gastric secretions, aiding the digestion of food.

items.title: Nausea relief
items.content: Warm ginger tea is commonly recommended for motion sickness, morning sickness, and postoperative nausea.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Caffeine from tea combined with ginger’s aroma can improve focus and increase alertness.

items.title: Blood sugar moderation
items.content: Studies suggest ginger may help modestly lower post‑meal glucose levels.

items.title: Ginger allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to ginger, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Ginger can enhance the effects of anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin) and increase bleeding risk.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: High amounts of ginger may irritate the stomach lining, causing heartburn or discomfort.

items.title: Pregnancy
items.content: Pregnant women should limit ginger intake to no more than 1 g per day unless advised by a healthcare professional.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steep 1‑2 teaspoons of ginger tea in 250 ml of hot water for 3‑5 minutes. Add honey, lemon, or milk if desired. It can be enjoyed hot or chilled.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bagged or loose tea in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Keep dried ginger separately in a tightly sealed jar.
